newsitem.title: UK: UK research needs high-tech link to compete-report.
newsitem.headline: UK research needs high-tech link to compete-report.

text.p: Britain needs to set up a network of high-tech links between company and university researchers if it is to remain competitive against the tiger economies of South East Asia, a report said on Monday.

A report by the Institution of Chemical Engineers called for the creation of "virtual research schools," allowing isolated research departments to share ideas through technological advances like the internet, video conferencing and direct computer links.
"Major advances usually spring from a mix of skills gleaned from various disciplines," the Institution said. "However, research in the UK tends to be organised in small specialist groups."

It said that increasingly, it is the speed with which new products can be brought to the customer that will dictate profitability. The UK will need to radically overhaul its research strategy to ensure a smooth and speedy transition from the laboratory to commerical production."
A spokeswoman said the Institution was not calling for addtional government funding, but for a change in the approach to research.
The Institution said Britain's research facilities were "stretched to the limit and, with a shortage of top level entrants into research, the situation is becoming worse."
